paper.title: CBSE Class 12 2023 · Chemistry · Set 56/1/2
paper.marking_note: Section A: +1 correct · no negative marking
paper.instructions:
(i) This question paper contains 35 questions. All questions are compulsory.
(ii) This question paper is divided into five Sections – A, B, C, D and E.
(iii) In Section A – Questions no. 1 to 18 are multiple choice (MCQ) type questions, carrying 1 mark each.
(iv) In Section B – Questions no. 19 to 25 very short answer (VSA) type questions, carrying 2 marks each.
(v) In Section C – Questions no. 26 to 30 are short answer (SA) type questions, carrying 3 marks each.
(vi) In Section D – Questions no. 31 and 32 are case-based questions carrying 4 marks each.
(vii) In Section E – Questions no. 33 to 35 are long answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each.
(viii) There is no overall choice. However, an internal choice has been provided in 2 questions in Section B, 2 questions in Section C, 2 questions in Section D and 2 questions in Section E.
(ix) Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.stem:
How would you account for : (2 × 1 = 2)
(a) The $E^{\circ}$ value for the $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}$ couple is much more positive than that for $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}$ couple or $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}$ couple.
(b) Complete the following equation :
$$\mathrm{2MnO_4^{-} + 16H^{+} + 5C_2O_4^{2-} \longrightarrow}$$
questions.solution:
(a) $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ changes to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ stable half-filled $d^{5}$ configuration / much larger third ionization enthalpy of Mn whereas $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ have stable configuration. (1)
(b) $$\mathrm{2MnO_4^{-} + 16H^{+} + 5C_2O_4^{2-} \longrightarrow 2Mn^{2+} + 10CO_2 + 8H_2O}$$ (1)

questions.stem:
Give reason : (3 × 1 = 3)
(a) Measurement of osmotic pressure method is preferred for the determination of molar masses of macromolecules such as proteins and polymers.
(b) Aquatic animals are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water.
(c) Elevation of boiling point of 1 M KCl solution is nearly double than that of 1 M sugar solution.
questions.solution:
(a) Osmotic pressure is measured at room temperature / molarity of the solution is used instead of molality / as compared to other colligative properties its magnitude is large even for a very dilute solution. (1)
(b) Solubility of oxygen is higher at a lower temperature. (1)
(c) KCl being strong electrolyte dissociates into two moles of ions but sugar will not dissociate / for KCl, $i = 2$ and for sugar, $i = 1$. (1)

questions.stem:

(iii) Carboxylic acids do not give characteristic reactions of carbonyl group.

questions.stem:
In coordination compounds, metals show two types of linkages, primary and secondary. Primary valencies are ionisable and are satisfied by negatively charged ions. Secondary valencies are non-ionisable and are satisfied by neutral or negative ions having lone pair of electrons. Primary valencies are non-directional while secondary valencies decide the shape of the complexes.

(i) If $\mathrm{PtCl_2 \cdot 2NH_3}$ does not react with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$, what will be its formula ? (1)
(ii) What is the secondary valency of $\mathrm{[Co(en)_3]^{3+}}$ ? (1)
(iii) (1) Write the formula of Iron(III)hexacyanidoferrate(II).
(2) Write the IUPAC name of $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]\,Cl_2}$. (2×1=2)
OR
(iii) Write the hybridization and magnetic behaviour of $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$. [Atomic number : Ni = 28] (2)

The rate of reaction is concerned with decrease in concentration of reactants or increase in the concentration of products per unit time. It can be expressed as instantaneous rate at a particular instant of time and average rate over a large interval of time. Mathematical representation of rate of reaction is given by rate law. Rate constant and order of a reaction can be determined from rate law or its integrated rate equation.

(i) What is average rate of reaction ? (1)
(ii) Write two factors that affect the rate of reaction. (1)
(iii) (1) What happens to rate of reaction for zero order reaction ?
(2) What is the unit of k for zero order reaction ? (2×1=2)
OR
(iii) (1) For a reaction $\mathrm{P + 2Q \longrightarrow Products}$
Rate $= k[\mathrm{P}]^{1/2}\,[\mathrm{Q}]^{1}$. What is the order of the reaction ?
(2) Define pseudo first order reaction with an example. (2×1=2)
questions.solution:
(i) Change in the concentration of a reactant or product per unit time. (1)
(ii) Concentration of reactants, Surface area, catalyst and temperature (any two). (1)
(iii) (1) rate is independent of the concentration of reactant(s) / rate remains constant / rate $= k$ (1)
(2) $\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}\ s^{-1}}$ (1)
OR
(iii) (1) $3/2$ / $1.5$ (1)
(2) A reaction that appears to be of higher order but follows first-order kinetics.
Example: Hydrolysis of an ester. (or any other correct example) (½ + ½)

questions.stem:
Assign reason for each of the following : (5×1=5)
(i) Manganese exhibits the highest oxidation state of $+7$ among the 3d series of transition elements.
(ii) Transition metals and their compounds are generally found to be good catalysts in chemical reactions.
(iii) $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ is reducing in nature while with the same d-orbital configuration ($d^{4}$) $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ is an oxidising agent.
(iv) Zn has lowest enthalpy of atomization.
(v) $\mathrm{Cu^{+}}$ is unstable in an aqueous solution.
questions.solution:
(i) Due to the participation of all 3d and 4s electrons in bond formation /due to the presence of maximum number of unpaired electrons. (1)
(ii) Due to variable oxidation state / due to the ability to adopt multiple oxidation states / due to the large surface area / due to complex formation. (1)
(iii) $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ changes from $d^{4}$ to stable half-filled $t_{2g}^{3}$ configuration while $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ changes to stable half-filled $d^{5}$ configuration. (1)
(iv) Due to the absence of unpaired electrons and weak interatomic interactions. (1)
(v) $\mathrm{Cu^{+}}$ ion (aq.) undergoes disproportionation to $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ (aq.) and Cu /
$\mathrm{2Cu^{+}(aq.) \longrightarrow Cu^{2+}(aq.) + Cu(s)}$ (1)

questions.stem:
(a) (i) State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. Write an expression for the molar conductivity of acetic acid at infinite dilution according to Kohlrausch's law.
(ii) Calculate the maximum work and $\log K_c$ for the given reaction at 298 K :
$\mathrm{Ni(s) + 2Ag^{+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons Ni^{2+}(aq) + 2Ag(s)}$
Given : $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ni^{2+}/Ni}} = -0.25\ \mathrm{V}$, $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Ag^{+}/Ag}} = +0.80\ \mathrm{V}$
$1\ \mathrm{F} = 96500\ \mathrm{C\ mol^{-1}}$ (2+3=5)
questions.solution:
(a) (i) Limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte can be represented as the sum of the individual contributions of the anion and cation of the electrolyte. (1)
$\Lambda^{\circ}_{m}(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}) = \lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{CH_3COO^{-}}} + \lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{H^{+}}}$ (1)
(ii) $\Delta_r G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}}$
Maximum work $= -\Delta_r G^{\circ} = nFE^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}}$ (½)
$= 2 \times 96500\ \mathrm{C\ mol^{-1}} \times (0.80 + 0.25)\ \mathrm{V}$
$= 2 \times 96500 \times 1.05\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$ (½)
$= 202{,}650\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$ or $202.65\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ (1)
$\log K_c = \dfrac{nE^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}}}{0.059}$ (½)
$= \dfrac{2 \times 1.05}{0.059} = 35.6$ (½)
questions.or_stem:
(b) (i) State Faraday's first law of electrolysis. How much charge, in terms of Faraday, is required for the reduction of 1 mol $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ to Cu ?
(ii) Calculate emf of the following cell at 298 K for
$\mathrm{Mg(s) \mid Mg^{2+}(0.1\ M) \parallel Cu^{2+}(0.01\ M) \mid Cu(s)}$
$[E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}} = +2.71\ \mathrm{V},\ 1\ \mathrm{F} = 96500\ \mathrm{C\ mol^{-1}},\ \log 10 = 1]$ (2+3=5)
questions.or_solution:
(b) (i) It states that the mass of a substance deposited /liberated at the electrodes is directly proportional to the charge/quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte. (1)
2F charge is required. (1)
(ii) $E_{\mathrm{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}]}$ (1)
$= 2.71\ \mathrm{V} - \dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{0.1}{0.01}$
$= 2.71\ \mathrm{V} - \dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log 10$ (1)
$= 2.71\ \mathrm{V} - 0.0295$
$= 2.68\ \mathrm{V}$ (1)
